A push to main publishes the token proxy image, makes a release and writes the gh-pages branch, and the context scalable-machine-runner-docs holds a token with Contents: Read and write on the whole repository, so a job of main could also push to main itself. The repository cannot protect main by itself. A ruleset is a setting of the GitHub repository, the signature of a release is only as good as it (What the release trust depends on), and the files of the repository cannot show that it is set. The maintainers have set the ruleset below on main (Settings, Rules, Rulesets, New branch ruleset, target: the default branch), and Check the settings says how to read it back:
Require a pull request before merging, with the number of reviews that you want. The release job never pushes a commit to main, so nobody and no job needs to. A required review from code owners adds nothing while .github/CODEOWNERS is the single line *: it asks the same people for every path, .circleci/ and ci/ included. Block force pushes and restrict deletions. No bypass list, not even for administrators. Require status checks to pass, with ONE check: the status of the workflow ci. Do not require anything else: GitHub gets one status for each workflow, not for each job. The workflows are ci, docs-site, the setup workflow of the branch (setup-e2e on main and smr-swarm/*, setup-plain elsewhere, setup-scan) and security-scan. A job name (lint-shell, docs-site-build, linux-swarm) is not a status, so a ruleset cannot require it. The setup workflow has a different name on different branches, so requiring setup-plain would block every pull request from smr-swarm/*, and the other way round. ci is on every pipeline, a docs-only one included, and it ends red when any job in it fails, so it stands for every lint and test job. Find the exact name of the status in a recent commit: gh api repos/CircleCI-Labs/scalable-machine-runner/commits/main/status --jq '.statuses[].context'.
data.cost-and-duration#Cost and duration:
Measured on 2026-10-13 (pipeline 9aed4106, a full run on smr-swarm/ci). Credits use the published per-minute rates (Windows medium 40, Linux xlarge 40, Linux medium and Arm medium 10, Docker small 5 and medium 10); the e2e probes run on the self-hosted classes and cost no compute credits.
Job Executor Duration setup and the small lint jobs Docker small 5 to 15 s each lint-powershell, lint-docs-mermaid Docker medium 56 s, 50 s e2e-simulation Linux VM medium 100 s linux-setup, linux-arm64 Linux VM medium, Arm medium 31 s, 29 s linux-image-example Linux VM medium 96 s linux-swarm (the whole Linux suite) Linux VM xlarge 7 min 14 s windows-swarm-ltsc2022 Windows 12 min 31 s windows-swarm-ltsc2025 Windows about 17 min e2e-linux-host (B1, B2, B3: 2 s each on the runner) Linux VM medium about 1.5 min e2e-windows-2022-host, -2025-host (B1, B2: 22 s each) Windows 7 min 30 s, 8 min Pipeline Credits (about) Wall clock Feature branch that changes a file that every heavy suite reads (the jobs of every pipeline, measured with both Windows jobs) 1,500, of which the two Windows jobs are 1,200 18 min The same branch now: the Server 2025 jobs run on main and with full: true only, and each heavy suite runs only for the files it reads (The heavy suites) 1,500 minus about 700 for the 2025 job, and minus about 500 when no Windows file changes 18 min main (every job except release) 3,800 25 min The measurements above predate the gating, and the second row is an estimate from them. Windows dominates the cost: every Windows job pulls the 2 GB Server Core image onto a fresh VM (about 5 to 10 minutes). A pull request that changes documentation only costs about 200 credits. The only schedule is the weekly security scan, about 150 credits a run.
data.create-the-schedule#Create the schedule:
The workflow runs when the pipeline parameter security-scan is true. Nothing in the repository creates the schedule: a maintainer does this once, with a token or in the web app. Use the branch main, so the scan reads the pins of main. The schedule below runs every Monday at 06:00 UTC, after Renovate has opened its pull requests (it runs before 06:00 UTC on Monday).
In the web app. Open the project, Project Settings, Project Setup (or Triggers). Next to the pipeline, select Schedule + and fill in the form:
Field Value Name weekly-security-scan Branch main Pipeline attribution The scheduling system Parameters security-scan = true Repeats Weekly, on Monday Start time (UTC) 06 Times per hour 1 Enable the trigger and save.
With the API. The CircleCI CLI has no command for schedules. Create a personal API token, keep it in CIRCLECI_TOKEN (never in a file of the repository, and never printed), and run:
curl --request POST "https://circleci.com/api/v2/project/gh/CircleCI-Labs/scalable-machine-runner/schedule" \ --header "circle-token: ${CIRCLECI_TOKEN}" \ --header "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{ "name": "weekly-security-scan", "description": "Trivy on every pinned image and govulncheck on the proxy (docs/ci.md, Security scan)", "attribution-actor": "system", "parameters": {"branch": "main", "security-scan": true}, "timetable": {"per-hour": 1, "hours-of-day": [6], "days-of-week": ["MON"]} }' To try it once before the first Monday, start a pipeline with the same parameter. Use the branch of the pull request to try a change, or main afterwards:
curl --request POST "https://circleci.com/api/v2/project/gh/CircleCI-Labs/scalable-machine-runner/pipeline" \ --header "circle-token: ${CIRCLECI_TOKEN}" \ --header "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{"branch": "main", "parameters": {"security-scan": true}}' The pipeline shows the workflow security-scan and the jobs security-scan-images and security-scan-go (and the setup job of the workflow setup-scan). With the scheduling system as the actor, CircleCI sends no failure e-mail to a person. To hear about a failed scan, add the project to the CircleCI Slack app (Project Settings, Notifications) or set attribution-actor to current so that the actor of the token gets the e-mail. To stop the scan, disable or delete the schedule in the same place.
data.deploys#Deploys:
The pipeline records its deployments in the Deploys view of CircleCI (Deploys in the web app), with deploy markers: circleci run release plan creates the deploy as pending, and circleci run release update moves it to RUNNING and then to SUCCESS or FAILED.
Deploy Job Component Environment Version A GitHub release release machine-runner-swarm github-releases The release tag, for example v0.2.0 The docs site docs-site-publish docs-site github-pages The commit SHA The token proxy image of a commit proxy-image-publish token-proxy-image docker-hub sha-<12 characters of the commit> The release tags of the image release token-proxy-image docker-hub The release number, X.Y.Z CircleCI creates the components and the environments on the first deploy: nobody sets them up. ci/deploy-marker.sh makes the calls, and ci/tests/deploy-marker.sh tests it in lint-circleci against a stub of the circleci command.
Only a real deploy is recorded. The release job plans its deploy after it has the version, and only when it will publish (GITHUB_TOKEN is set). Nothing to release and a run without the token record nothing. The docs job records a deploy only with GITHUB_TOKEN as well, because without it nothing is published, and the image jobs record theirs only with the Docker Hub credentials. Failure. The release script gives the deploy the status FAILED, with the exit status as the reason, on every way out of the script: a failed check, a failed signature, a failed gh call. A failed or canceled deploy gives the live version back to the last successful one in the Deploys view. The docs job does the same in a step with when: on_fail, with a link to the job as the reason. Cancel. A cancel that reaches ci/release.sh as a signal records CANCELED. The long step of docs-site-publish and of proxy-image-publish runs under ci/deploy-marker.sh guard NAME COMMAND, which stops the command on SIGTERM or SIGINT, gives the deploy CANCELED and exits 143. A canceled step runs no later step (not even one with when: on_fail), so without the guard the deploy would stay RUNNING. Whether CircleCI sends the signal to the step is the one thing that only a real cancel shows: the script and its test (ci/tests/deploy-marker.sh) cover the rest. The plan comes after the build. docs-site-publish builds the site first and plans its deploy afterwards, so a site that does not build is a failed job and not a FAILED deploy. One job. Plan and updates are steps of one job. A rerun from failed that starts a new job would break the link between them, and CircleCI refuses a second final status for a deploy. A marker never fails a job. If the task agent refuses a call (for example the organization has no Deploys), the script prints a warning and exits 0.
data.docs-site#Docs site:
The documentation is also a site on GitHub Pages: https://circleci-labs.github.io/scalable-machine-runner/. CircleCI builds it with Hugo and the Hextra theme and pushes it to the gh-pages branch. No GitHub Actions workflow is involved. The Markdown of README.md, docs/, CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTING.md stays the only source, and nothing in it is written for the site: README.md is the home page.
Path What it is site/hugo.yaml The Hugo configuration: baseURL, the menu, the “not officially supported” banner, search and Mermaid site/go.mod, site/go.sum Pin the Hextra module site/nav.txt The order, the groups and the sidebar labels of the pages site/stage.sh Copies the Markdown into site/content/ (generated, not tracked) and leaves the sources unchanged site/check.sh lychee, offline, on the built site: links and heading anchors site/publish.sh Pushes the built site to gh-pages site/preview.sh Builds the pull request preview with relative URLs and prints its address site/preview-comment.sh Posts or updates one comment with that address on the pull request (optional)
data.docs-site-previews#Docs site previews:
docs-site-build runs on every pipeline, so every branch and pull request gets a preview of its site, and writes its address into a workspace for docs-site-comment. The production build links to its pages under /scalable-machine-runner/, so it can work only at the GitHub Pages address. CircleCI serves the artifacts of a job from https://output.circle-artifacts.com/output/job//artifacts//, and the job id is new on every run. site/preview.sh therefore builds a second copy, site/public-preview, that works from any address:
Hugo builds it with relative URLs (a link from docs/maintainers/ci.html to the home page is ../../index.html) and with uglyURLs, so that a page is a file (ci.html). The script then makes every relative link name a file: a server of artifacts does not serve the index.html of a directory, and the menu links to directories. It also rewrites the url(/fonts/...) of the inline style, and removes the integrity attributes: CircleCI sends script and style files to storage on another origin, and a browser refuses a script with an integrity hash from there. lychee then checks the links and the anchors of the preview with directory links turned off, and the script stops on a link that begins with a slash. The GitHub links of the pages point at the commit of the build, so a file that the pull request adds has a link that works. The job stores the preview as the artifacts docs-site-preview, and prints and stores the address:
Docs preview: https://output.circle-artifacts.com/output/job//artifacts/0/docs-site-preview/index.html The same line is in the file docs-site/preview-url.txt among the artifacts of the job. CircleCI has no job summary page, so the log line, that file and the Artifacts tab are the places to look. Who can open the link follows the visibility of the project on CircleCI, and the artifacts expire (30 days by default). Search and the Mermaid diagrams load files by absolute path and may not work from the artifacts. To see the exact site, download docs-site.tgz or run the commands of Preview locally.
A comment on the pull request (optional). docs-site-build has no context, so no token is in the environment of Hugo, lychee, the Go modules or the scripts of site/, and a pipeline that an API call starts (for example with full: true) is never refused for the restriction of a context that it does not use. A second job, docs-site-comment, holds the context scalable-machine-runner-pr-comments. It requires docs-site-build, takes the address from its workspace, and runs only for a push that has a pull request (the setup phase passes pull-request: true when CIRCLE_PULL_REQUEST is a GitHub pull request address). It is not a requirement of the release: lint-circleci lists it as optional. When the job has a GITHUB_PR_COMMENT_TOKEN, site/preview-comment.sh posts ONE comment with the address, and updates that comment on later pushes (it finds it by a hidden marker, and posts a new one only if the update fails). Without the token, without a pull request (CircleCI sets CIRCLE_PULL_REQUEST only when the branch has one at the time of the push), or when GitHub refuses a call, it skips the comment and the job stays green. It sends the token to curl on its standard input, so the token is in no command line and no log. ci/tests/preview-comment.sh tests all of this against a fake curl.
To turn the comment on, a maintainer does this once:
Create a fine-grained personal access token for a dedicated bot account that is on no bypass list and has no other access, with the resource owner CircleCI-Labs, only this repository, and the repository permission Issues: Read and write, and nothing else. A comment on a pull request is an issue comment, and site/preview-comment.sh calls only the issue comment endpoints, so the token needs no pull request permission. Do not use the token of a maintainer: Pull requests: Read and write would also let the token submit approving reviews and edit or close pull requests, as its owner.
Create the context scalable-machine-runner-pr-comments with the variable GITHUB_PR_COMMENT_TOKEN. The docs-site-comment job already names the context. Without the variable the job posts nothing.
Restrict the context to this project, and refuse SSH reruns:
circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-pr-comments --org --type project --value circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-pr-comments --org --type expression \ --value 'not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")' The context cannot be limited to one branch: pull requests come from branches of any name. So anyone who can push a branch to the repository can make a job print the token. That is why the token has the one permission above, belongs to a bot account, and is not the release token: whoever reads it can write to issues and to the comments of pull requests as that bot, and cannot submit a review or merge. A pull request from a fork gets no secret (Secrets and public logs), so it gets no comment.
data.documentation-only-changes#Documentation:
A pull request that changes only documentation runs the lint jobs and the docs site build, and skips the builds, the Swarm tests, the Windows jobs, the e2e and the release. The setup job runs ci/changed-files.sh after checkout, and ci/setup-gate.sh decides from its answer. A change is documentation when every path is under docs/ or site/, or is a Markdown file anywhere (README.md, CHANGELOG.md, *.md). The exception is docs/microvm.md: linux/tests/microvm.sh reads its Docker configuration from it, so a change to it runs everything.
Which commits. On a branch: everything since the merge base with origin/main, so a push that holds only a docs commit still runs the full pipeline when an earlier commit of the same pull request changed code. On main: everything since the commit of the build that ran before (the pipeline value pipeline.git.base_revision), so a push of several commits is judged as a whole. When it is not known, everything runs. The first build of a branch, a pipeline started through the API, a base that the clone does not hold, a failed git fetch and an empty list all mean “not known”. The pipeline parameter full: true also turns the shortcut off. The release gate stays whole. docs-only turns release off together with the e2e flags, because the release requires every job and those jobs do not run. That is safe because cliff.toml makes no release for a commit of the type docs, test, ci, chore, style, refactor or build. It does release for fix(docs):, feat(docs): and any breaking change (docs!: or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer), because the docs ship in the release bundle. So on main the gate asks ci/changed-files.sh --releasable (it reads the skip pattern from cliff.toml): when a commit of the push would make a release, docs-only stays false and the whole pipeline runs, with the release. The answer errs towards a release. A docs: push that the release job would have ended as Nothing to release is the only one that loses a job. Publishing continues. The workflow docs-site is not affected: a docs change on main is published and recorded as a deploy. Required checks. GitHub gets one status for each workflow, not one for each job, and a docs-only pipeline still ends the workflow ci green. Require the status of the workflow ci and nothing else (A ruleset for main). ci/tests/setup-gate.sh has the table of rows (paths, branch, releasable, full), and ci/tests/changed-files.sh runs the script on throwaway repositories: a push of several commits, a base that is not known, a shallow clone, and one commit of each type against cliff.toml. lint-circleci also checks that every job of ci that is not a lint job or docs-site-build has a filter that a docs-only change turns off.
A pipeline of main or smr-swarm/* that is started through the API, or an SSH rerun of such a job, is refused by the context restriction (below): its setup job fails with an authorization error. Start the full suite on another branch with full: true instead, or push a commit.
Why the gate is in the setup phase. A guard job that runs circleci-agent step halt is not enough on its own.
The probe jobs target a self-hosted runner class. Once a pipeline schedules them, they queue until a runner claims them, and CircleCI keeps runner jobs queued for days. Halting a guard job ends only that job, so the probes would still be scheduled. The decision therefore has to happen before the e2e jobs are compiled into the workflow. The setup job also calls the continuation API itself, rather than through the circleci/continuation orb, because the orb prints the request body, and with it the continuation key, into a public log.
data.e2e-a-runner-hosted-inside-a-circleci-jo: Both e2e groups follow one pattern. Job A (the host, a cloud VM with the context attached) installs the stack and hosts the runner as a Swarm service for the resource class cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-. The probe jobs (B) are ordinary jobs on that class, without the context. B1 leaves residue, B2 is scheduled after B1 and must find a different container and none of the residue. A verifies independently of the probes, from docker events, and prints the verdict.
data.facts-about-the-ci-machines-that-the-des:
These were measured on 2026-10-12 and shaped the scripts. Check them first when something Swarm-related breaks in CI.
Fact Consequence Linux machine image ubuntu-2604:2026.05.1: Docker 29.4.2 with the containerd image store (overlayfs snapshotter), on x86_64 and on arm64 The writable layer is upperdir=/var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/N/fs; the probes hash it A service with hostname: "{{.Node.Hostname}}--{{.Task.Slot}}" (the shipped Linux stack) gives every container of a slot the same hostname Probes cannot use the hostname. They read the full container ID from /proc/self/mountinfo (Docker bind-mounts /etc/hostname from /var/lib/docker/containers//) and compare the writable-layer hash. The host maps the container ID to the Nth start event of the service docker events prints an empty exitCode for start events The event format uses {{or (index .Actor.Attributes "exitCode") "-"}}, or the columns shift Windows machine images (Server 2022 build 20348, Server 2025 build 26100): Docker 29.4.0, default isolation process Containers share the host kernel; the node must carry machine-runner-swarm.windows-=true for the stack’s placement constraint (a Server 2025 node carries both windows-ltsc2022 and windows-ltsc2025) docker swarm init on a Windows machine image fails with could not find the system's IP address - specify one with --advertise-addr Pass --advertise-addr with the IPv4 address of the Ethernet adapter (the vEthernet (nat) adapter has a 172.x address). The Windows jobs and the documentation do this For a few seconds after docker swarm init on a Windows VM, outbound connections and DNS fail (Unable to connect to the remote server, lookup mcr.microsoft.com: no such host) Every Windows job downloads and pulls first, and runs docker swarm init last The CircleCI Windows image has PsExec64.exe on the host’s PATH The task agent would use a desktop wrapper if it were on the container’s PATH. The host’s PATH never reaches the containers: the stack sets theirs in full, windows\Setup.ps1 ignores the host’s PsExec, and an image build checks only the image’s own PATH In Windows PowerShell 5.1, piping a string to a native command appends CR LF The Windows host writes the runner config with [IO.File]::WriteAllText into a file that exists only while docker secret create reads it On Windows a Swarm secret is a file under C:\ProgramData\Docker\secrets, readable by Administrators and SYSTEM only; jobs run as ContainerAdministrator A job can read the runner config, so the token, on Windows. The probe records this instead of asserting a protection. The token is not in the job environment: the runner reads it from the config file docker stop and docker service update end a stock Server Core container about 5 seconds after the shutdown event (HCS waits only WaitToKillServiceTimeout; exit code 3221225786, 0xC000013A), whatever it is running Every Windows service runs the stock image, and no image is built. Test-StopHandling.ps1 measures the rule (an informational NOTE control line: the job is killed after a stop), and the e2e no longer stops a busy container. A job that finishes ends its container cleanly, which is what the e2e checks. The DIY image that lifts the limit is in Stop a busy Windows container and is not tested here Pulling mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2022 (about 2.2 GB compressed) onto a fresh Windows VM takes about 10 minutes Every Windows job pays it, in a step of its own with no_output_timeout: 30m; it is most of the cost (below) A Windows host runs images of its own release and older ones: a 2025 host also runs ltsc2022 images, a 2022 host cannot run ltsc2025 images (0xc0370101), and nested virtualisation is not available, so only process isolation works The Windows jobs pick the image tag from the host’s build number (20348: ltsc2022, 26100: ltsc2025) The Android machine image (android:current) supports nested virtualization (documented), and no other CircleCI image does: the Windows hosts and the other Linux images have no /dev/kvm and no Hyper-V isolation Only linux-microvm runs on it. A microvm.sh that finds no /dev/kvm skips locally and fails there (SWARM_TEST_REQUIRE_KVM=1) A CircleCI step shell starts with SIGHUP ignored Nothing here relies on SIGHUP
data.github-pages-and-the-token#GitHub Pages:
A maintainer does this once:
Create the context scalable-machine-runner-docs with the variable GITHUB_TOKEN: a fine-grained token for this repository only, with the repository permission Contents: read and write and nothing else. Without the variable the job builds and checks the site and publishes nothing, as the release does without its token.
Restrict the context like the e2e context (Secrets and public logs), to this project and to main:
circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-docs --org --type project --value circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-docs --org --type expression \ --value 'pipeline.git.branch == "main" and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")' After the first publication, open Settings, Pages, and set Source to Deploy from a branch, the branch to gh-pages and the folder to / (root). GitHub then deploys every push to that branch with its own managed pages-build-deployment run. There is no workflow file to maintain.
The site has its own context and not the release context. The two tokens have the same scope, Contents: Read and write on the repository, and the docs job downloads and runs a theme, a Mermaid script and a Hugo binary at build time while it holds its token (What each job can see). The context limits which job can use the token, not what the token can do, and the ruleset on main is what keeps it from changing main. A token that belongs to a bot account on no bypass list is safer than one that belongs to a maintainer. If one token for both is wanted, attach scalable-machine-runner-release to docs-site-publish instead: that context holds a GITHUB_TOKEN that can write to the repository, and no other change is needed.
When the repository is renamed to machine-runner-swarm, the Pages address changes with it and GitHub does not redirect the old one. Change the two lines of site/hugo.yaml that name the repository (baseURL and the GitHub link of the menu). The publication follows the repository that the pipeline runs in.
data.jobs-and-why-there-are-two#Jobs and why:
Job Workflow When What docs-site-build ci every pipeline Stage, hugo --minify --panicOnWarning and site/check.sh, then the preview. No context. The release requires it docs-site-comment ci a push that has a pull request The optional comment with the preview address, in a job of its own with the context that holds the token. The release does not wait for it docs-site-publish docs-site main only The same build steps, then site/publish.sh, and a deploy marker lint-circleci fails when a job of ci that no other job requires is not a requirement of the release. A publication in ci would therefore make every release wait for it, and a failed publication would block a release. The publication is a job of its own workflow, docs-site, on main. It rebuilds the site with the same docs-site command and does not wait for the other tests, because the pages describe main. serial-group allows one publication at a time.
site/publish.sh replaces everything on gh-pages with site/public, adds .nojekyll, and commits only when something changed. The first run creates the branch without a parent. The commit message ends with [skip ci], so the push starts no pipeline. The commit contains the bytes as built: the pages carry integrity hashes for their scripts, and the script switches off every line-ending conversion of git.
data.linux#Linux:
e2e-linux (job group, serial-group /e2e-linux) e2e-linux-host (A) ci/e2e-host.sh prepare | run | cleanup | sweep e2e-linux-b1 (B1) service linux-default e2e-linux-b2 (B2) service linux-default, requires B1; holds 75 s while the host restarts the token proxy e2e-linux-b3 (B3) service linux-hardened, requires B2 e2e-linux-arm64 (job group, the same serial-group, requires e2e-linux) e2e-linux-arm64-host and -b1, -b2, -b3: the same on arm.medium Host.
prepare is sudo linux/setup.sh --swarm-init (a manager, where the token proxy runs with no label), the documented path: the shipped runner-distributor runs in the stack and installs the runner. It also builds the token proxy image of the checkout (docker build proxy/) on the VM, which is the only node, because this job has no registry: run deploys the shipped stack with MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE set to it. run creates the two secrets linux-default-token and linux-hardened-token from E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_LINUX through setup.sh --secret, and the placeholder runner-placeholder-token that the runners read. The token proxy mounts the two class secrets, so the real token reaches the real API only through it. Each secret is a runner config file (api.auth_token), the target is circleci_runner_config.yaml, owned by uid 2000 with mode 0400. The token travels on stdin, never in a file or on a command line. The stack’s other secret gets a placeholder. It deploys the shipped linux/stack/runners.yaml (the optional classes live in docker-build.yaml and persistent.yaml and are not deployed) with a generated override that gives the active service one replica of a digest-pinned stock cimg/base, a 5 minute idle timeout, and a bind mount for the evidence directory; every other runner service gets zero replicas. The runner-distributor stays as shipped and installs the pinned release of CircleCI from the real manifest, and the runner service waits up to 10 minutes for it. The runner and the entrypoint come through the stack’s own read-only volume runner-bin and the Swarm config of the entrypoint. Phase 1 is linux-default (the job user keeps sudo) for B1 and B2. While B2 holds its job (the probe sleeps 75 s first), the host restarts the token proxy, and B2 must pass: this runs the real runner and the real task agent through a proxy restart against the real API, and the restart must restore the runner that claimed (the start line says state restored and 1 runner(s) have claimed for the class). When B2 reports, the host removes the stack at once, so that its replacement container cannot claim the next probe. Phase 2 is linux-hardened (MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO=false) for B3. Both services use the same class token, so only one is deployed at a time. Probes (ci/e2e-probe.sh):
The first step checks that /e2e-evidence/host names this workflow: a probe claimed by a stray runner fails there. Residue: B1 plants files in $HOME, /tmp, /var/tmp and (with sudo) /etc; every probe fails if it finds an earlier probe’s files. Identity: the container ID (from /proc/self/mountinfo) and the writable layer hash must differ from the previous probe’s. The step-down is checked too: the job runs as circleci (the image’s user), the runner as circleci-runner, the entrypoint logged stepdown=sudo for the default service and stepdown=setpriv no_new_privs=yes for the hardened one, and sudo -n true works in the default service only. This is the first real check of jobs through the sudo -niHu circleci -- prefix and through the setpriv --no-new-privs prefix of the hardened class. Token readability, recorded in the evidence and printed in the verdict. As the job user, without and with sudo, it tries to read /run/secrets/circleci_runner_config.yaml (only byte counts are kept, never the content), it counts other users’ /proc/PID/environ that it can read, and it checks the job environment, every process’s command line and, through sudo, the runner’s environment for the token’s variable and key names (names only, never values). The token must be in none of them. A read without sudo must fail in both services. In the hardened service sudo must be unusable and the token unreadable with it; in the default service the sudo outcome is recorded and not asserted, because root can read the token. Each probe’s last step writes passed or failed to /e2e-evidence/..status, so the host stops at once on a failed probe. Verdict (ci/e2e-host.sh). It requires:
three containers with distinct IDs and exit code 0, each the one that Swarm started for its probe (the container ID in the evidence equals the Nth start event of that service); distinct writable layers, and residue=[] for every probe; the entrypoint’s step-down in the runner log, sudo for the default class and setpriv with no_new_privs=yes for the hardened class, job user circleci and runner user circleci-runner in every probe; B3 without working sudo, and no probe able to read the token without sudo. It prints, for example:
RESULT e2e=linux probes=3 distinct_containers=3 b2_residue=[] job_user=circleci runner_user=circleci-runner stepdown=hardened:setpriv,default:sudo token_in_job_env=absent token_on_command_line=absent token_default_nosudo=denied token_default_sudo=readable runner_env_via_sudo_default=no token_hardened_nosudo=denied token_hardened_sudo=no-sudo hardened_sudo_works=no verdict=PASS
data.linux-jobs-without-a-token#Linux jobs wi:
linux-swarm runs the Linux suite and needs no secret. linux-setup and linux-arm64 run ci/linux-smoke.sh on a fresh VM:
linux/setup.sh --check, then --swarm-init twice (the second run must be a no-op). The shipped stack is deployed by setup.sh --deploy with a made-up token (the runner gets 401 from CircleCI, which does not matter here). Nothing is installed by hand: the runner-distributor service downloads the pinned release of CircleCI from CircleCI’s real manifest, and the job waits for its link current. The volume runner-bin is root-owned and not writable by others, its record SHA256 equals the hash of the binary, and /opt/machine-runner-swarm does not exist on the host. The runner reports its version unmodified inside a stock cimg/base through -v runners_runner-bin:/opt/machine-runner-swarm:ro, the container’s architecture equals the host’s, the runner binary is built for it (file), and circleci-runner-entrypoint with a config file but no runner name exits 80. Inside the running linux-default and linux-hardened containers: the runner runs as circleci-runner; the container mounts only the placeholder config, the job user cannot read /run/secrets/circleci_runner_config.yaml, nor any other user’s process environment; linux-default keeps sudo, and sudo can read the placeholder config (the class token is in the token proxy, which this test stops); linux-hardened has no sudo at all. linux-image-example builds the bring-your-own-image example and scans it. Trivy policy:
The SBOM (CycloneDX) and the HIGH/CRITICAL reports of the image are artifacts: reports/sbom-example.cdx.json, reports/trivy-example.{json,txt}. The gate fails on a fixable CRITICAL finding that the image adds on top of cimg/base (the same scan of the base image is subtracted). The base is upstream: it bundles Docker, Compose and yq with their own findings, and those stay visible in the reports. What this repository owns is what it puts on top, the example’s packages. The runner is not in the image. Exceptions go in .trivyignore, one CVE per line, with a reason, an owner and an exp: date. Trivy stops honouring an entry after that date. An exception is only for findings that this repository cannot fix.
data.linux-microvm#linux-microvm:
linux-microvm runs linux/tests/microvm.sh on the Android machine image, because it is the only CircleCI machine image with nested virtualization. The job loads vhost_vsock and vhost_net, installs zstd, and runs the script with SWARM_TEST_REQUIRE_KVM=1, so a missing /dev/kvm fails the job instead of skipping the test. The script downloads the pinned Kata release and checks its SHA-256, starts a runc manager and a Kata worker in Docker-in-Docker containers, and deploys the real runners.yaml and microvm.yaml with the real entrypoint, the real runner against a fake API, and a fake runner. Refer to MicroVM jobs for the checks.
The job passes on CircleCI: the Android image has /dev/kvm, /dev/vhost-vsock, and a Docker that runs privileged containers, and the job was green in each of the first three pipelines that ran it, so it is in the release requirements like every job of the workflow. Run the same script locally on any host with KVM; it skips without /dev/kvm.

Checkout, caches and artifacts over virtiofs are not exercised Real jobs on arm64 The e2e group e2e-linux-arm64 runs the same three probes on a real arm64 runner, which the distributor installed on an Arm VM. linux-arm64 is the smoke test before it: the install by the distributor and the start of the stack A mirror over https with a private certificate authority, and a download through a proxy The distributor test serves its mirror over plain HTTP, and linux-setup downloads from the real bucket over https RHEL and SELinux The steps follow Docker’s documentation Rerun job with SSH (ssh-rerun.yaml) CI checks that the files parse and merge and keep the contract, including the host-mode port 54782, max_replicas_per_node: 1 and the advertise address. The Swarm side was proven by hand on a Linux Swarm with a real runner: the Enable SSH step runs, and the task agent answers on port 54782 of the node. No test logs in over SSH, and the Windows file is untested Windows Server 2019, Hyper-V isolation, group managed service accounts, proxies, and add_ssh_keys Not exercised, and the docs say so CircleCI server, and a runner version other than the pin The tests use CircleCI cloud, a fake API, and the exact pin of the stack files. The protocol that the proxy relies on is in Compatibility with CircleCI The two distributors reaching the same decision The shell distributor and the PowerShell distributor repeat the version grammar, the hash-list rules, the record format and the pruning. Each has its own tests, and nothing runs both on the same input. They differ in two places that are known: the Linux flip of current is one atomic rename, and the Windows flip removes the link and creates it again, so a container that starts in between does not start and Swarm retries (Upgrade the runner on Windows); file:// is accepted on Windows only The settings that the stack files repeat YAML anchors do not cross files, so the add-on files repeat the common blocks (restart policy, ulimits, logging, environment). stack-config.sh checks the pin and the hash list in every file, the contract of the services it names, and that ssh-rerun.yaml differs from linux-default only in the SSH settings. It does not check that every other repeated setting is identical, so such a drift is found by review publish() of the release job It stops before publishing without GITHUB_TOKEN, so the first release is its first real run. The signing, the verification and the check of the ref in the certificate are not part of that gap: signing-rehearsal runs them in every pipeline on a throwaway image. The push to Docker Hub, the tags, the GitHub release and the gh-pages push are real only on main
data.pinned-versions#Pinned versions:
Every tool image is pinned by tag and digest, and every download by version and SHA-256 value. Renovate, the GitHub App of the organization, keeps them current. renovate.json is its whole configuration: the repository needs no workflow or token for it, and no GitHub Actions workflow is involved.
When. Renovate opens pull requests on Monday before 06:00 UTC, at most six at a time. A major version waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard (the issue that Renovate keeps). Groups. One pull request for each group: CI images, stack images, proxy image bases, CI tools, Go toolchain, Windows distributor tools, lychee (the image and the binary move together) and docs site theme. Commit types. A pull request that changes what users run (stack images, proxy image bases, Go toolchain for the proxy image, Windows distributor tools) is a fix(deps) commit, so the release job makes a release for it. proxy image bases is the base images of the token proxy image: the distroless base of proxy/Dockerfile and the Nano Server digests of ci/Build-ProxyImage.ps1. A new digest of a base would otherwise be ci(deps), which cliff.toml skips, and the published image would keep stale base layers until an unrelated feat or fix lands. The CI-only groups are ci(deps) and the theme is docs(deps): they make no release (Releasing). Digests. Renovate pins every image that carries a digest, refreshes the digest of a tag, and moves the tag and the digest together. cimg/base and the e2e sweeper image circleci/runner-agent get a new digest but never a new tag: the tag is named in the stack files, the tests and the docs, or moves with the runner build, so a person changes it. Pin Where How Renovate finds it Images with a digest .circleci/*.yml, linux/stack/*.yaml, windows/stack/*.yaml, ci/, the tests, the docs One regex manager for name:tag@sha256:... in any file Hugo, lychee, the CircleCI CLI docs-site command and lint-circleci in .circleci/continue.yml A # renovate: comment above the version variable git-cliff, cosign, crane, gh, Go, govulncheck ci/release.sh, ci/tools.sh (cosign, crane), ci/security-scan.sh The same comment yamllint lint-yaml A regex for yamllint==X (PyPI) Kata Containers KATA_VERSION in linux/tests/microvm.sh A regex (GitHub releases) PortableGit, 7-Zip ReleaseTag and SevenZipVersion in windows/stack/runner-distributor.ps1 A regex each (GitHub releases) Node.js of the Windows example image NODE_VERSION in windows/images/example/Dockerfile, kept on the 24 line A regex (Node.js releases) The Hextra theme site/go.mod, site/go.sum The gomod manager The proxy module proxy/go.mod The gomod manager. It has no dependency today. The go directive is the oldest Go that can build it, so Renovate leaves it alone To pin a new tool, put its version in one variable and add the comment # renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=/ extractVersion=^v(?.*)$ on the line above it. The comment is the whole configuration.
data.pins-that-stay-by-hand#Pins that stay by:
Renovate does not touch these. Change the version and its checksum together, and run the check of the job that uses it.
Images without a digest in the stack files (coredns/coredns, alpine:3.24 of the token proxy, the cimg classes) and the Windows servercore tags: the tag is a choice for users, and Windows tags must match the host. The weekly security scan still scans them (not the Windows images). The Linux and Windows machine images (executors in .circleci/continue.yml): ubuntu-2604:2026.05.1, windows-server-2022-gui:2026.05.1 and windows-server-2025-gui:2026.05.1. They use dated tags and not current, which CircleCI moves every three months: an image that changes under an unrelated pull request would turn it red. Renovate cannot update them. Every quarter, read the image changelog, move those three tags together, and start a pipeline for the branch with full: true. The Android machine image for linux-microvm: android:current. CircleCI publishes quarterly tags plus current (gen2) and default (gen1), not dated tags on the ubuntu cadence. Renovate cannot update it; bump it by hand when the image changelog says to. PSScriptAnalyzer and Pester (lint-powershell, windows-swarm, windows/tests/Invoke-UnitTests.ps1). The Mermaid script of the site (params.mermaid.base in site/hugo.yaml): it must match the version that the lint-docs-mermaid image bundles. data.pipeline-shape#Pipeline shape:
There is one workflow, ci, and a small second one, docs-site, that publishes the documentation site on main (Docs site). Every job of both is listed in .circleci/continue.yml. The setup job passes twelve boolean parameters, and expression filters (filters: pipeline.parameters.) switch jobs in and out, so a job that does not apply is never scheduled. The setup phase itself has three mutually exclusive workflows that run the same setup job: setup-e2e for main and smr-swarm/*, with the e2e context, setup-plain for every other branch, without any context, and setup-scan for the weekly scan, without any context either (below).

data.preview-locally#Preview locally:
Install Hugo extended 0.168.0 and Go (Hugo downloads the theme as a Go module), then run from the repository root:
site/stage.sh cd site && hugo server Run site/stage.sh again after you change a page. To run the check of the pipeline, add lychee and run (cd site && hugo --minify --panicOnWarning) && site/check.sh.
data.publishing-fails-closed-on-main#Publishi:
A missing publishing credential must not leave main green with nothing published. The setup gate sets the pipeline parameter strict to true for main when both e2e tokens are present, which is the production project (the same condition as release, and a documentation-only change does not turn it off). The jobs that publish get it as REQUIRE_CREDENTIALS=true: proxy-image-linux and proxy-image-windows (the publish variants, in a first step, before the long build), proxy-image-publish, proxy-image-edge, release and docs-site-publish. When DOCKERHUB_USERNAME, DOCKERHUB_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN is missing, renamed, emptied or kept from the job by a context restriction, the job fails with a message that names the context.
Everywhere else the publication is skipped with a message and the pipeline stays green, as before: a project that has not created the contexts yet, a fork of this repository, and any branch. ci/tests/require-credentials.sh tests both behaviors, and the table test of the gate has a row for strict.
data.release#Release:
The release job is part of the ci workflow. On main, when both e2e tokens are present, the setup phase passes release: true together with full-suite, the three heavy suites, e2e-linux and e2e-windows, so every job that the release requires really runs. The job requires every other job of the workflow except the three optional ones that lint-circleci names in its $optional list (linux-mixed-arch, proxy-image-edge and docs-site-comment), and the release waits for every test. Pipelines of other branches never run it, and neither do tag pipelines (the release creates the tag; CircleCI schedules no job for a tag).
Job Executor What it does release cimg/base:2026.10, contexts scalable-machine-runner-release and scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub, serial-group ci/release.sh: the check of the Swarm config names, version, notes, the digest of the token proxy image pinned in the stack files, bundles, SHA256SUMS, keyless signature, the signature check and the release tags of the image, GitHub release. Without GITHUB_TOKEN or without the Docker Hub credentials it stops before publishing Add a new job to requires of the release job. lint-circleci fails when a job of the workflow is missing from it: it compiles the workflow and checks that every job that no other job requires is a requirement of the release (in the compiled workflow the release waits for one lock job, which requires them). Refer to Releasing for the rules, the setup of the token, and how to recover from a failed release.

data.secrets-and-public-logs#Secrets and publ:
The project is public, so job logs and artifacts are public.
The runner tokens live only in the scalable-machine-runner-e2e context, and only the setup job of the setup-e2e workflow and the host jobs attach it. Its restrictions are this project and an expression that allows only the branches that may use it, an SSH rerun excluded, and a pipeline started through the API excluded:
(pipeline.git.branch == "main" or pipeline.git.branch starts-with "smr-swarm/") and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api") A restriction of the context is a setting of the CircleCI organization, and the config file cannot change it, so a maintainer sets it. With the CLI, where is the organization slug and is 7bbdbb66-6ba8-4f6c-982e-d4fb401ec257:
circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-e2e --org --type project --value circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-e2e --org --type expression \ --value '(pipeline.git.branch == "main" or pipeline.git.branch starts-with "smr-swarm/") and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")' The expression is the second line of defence: the when of the setup workflows already keeps the context out of every other branch, and the restriction keeps an API pipeline (which can name any branch and, where the organization allows it, bring its own config) from using it. In the organization’s advanced settings, leave pipelines with an unversioned config off.
Project settings. The project is connected through the GitHub OAuth integration, not the GitHub App. Its slug is gh/CircleCI-Labs/scalable-machine-runner, not circleci//. The settings Build forked pull requests and Pass secrets to builds from forked pull requests (Project Settings, Advanced) exist for OAuth projects, and both must be off: a fork pull request would otherwise run its own .circleci/config.yml on this project. Also turn on the setting that requires an administrator to change project settings, and turn off SSH reruns, if the organization offers them. Auto-cancel redundant workflows must be off (Project Settings, Advanced): with it on, every push to smr-swarm/* or to any branch that is not the default cancels the e2e workflow that is running, and the host of a cancelled workflow can leave a Swarm service that claims the next pipeline’s job. The e2e workflows of two pushes then fail each other. With it off, the serial-group of each group lets one run at a time and the newer one waits.
On Linux the token goes to docker secret create on stdin and is never on disk. On Windows it is in a file for the instant docker secret create reads it, outside the artifact directory. It is never printed.
The probes never print their environment, and read the token only to count bytes.
The context is attached only to setup and the host jobs. The probes are ordinary runner jobs.
data.security-scan#Security scan:
A weekly workflow, security-scan, looks for known vulnerabilities in what the repository pins. It is a workflow of its own in .circleci/continue.yml, started by a schedule trigger, and it never runs the ci workflow: no build, no e2e job and no release. It has no context, so it holds no secret.
Job Executor What it does security-scan-images ubuntu-2604:2026.05.1, Docker ci/security-scan.sh images: Trivy on every image that the repository pins, in two lists: an infra image fails on a CRITICAL finding with a fix, and the other images are only reported. The script finds them in the files: every reference with a digest (name:tag@sha256:...: the CI jobs, the tests, the stack files) and the image: of every stack file, so the cimg classes, CoreDNS and alpine:3.24 are in too. Trivy pulls each image from its registry (--image-src remote) and builds nothing security-scan-go golang:1.27.2, small ci/security-scan.sh go: govulncheck on proxy/ with the Go toolchain of the proxy builds. It fails on any vulnerability that the proxy calls (a standard library fix means a new Go release) Two lists of images. ci/security-scan-images.txt is the one place that says how an image is treated, by repository name:
infra: what a stack runs as infrastructure on a user’s cluster, today alpine (the distributor), ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy (the token proxy, the tag edge that the stack files name: until the first publication the scan reports that it cannot pull it) and coredns/coredns (the microVM DNS forwarder). A CRITICAL finding with a fix fails security-scan-images, and so does an infra image that Trivy cannot scan. report: the job images that users choose (cimg/*, which the CircleCI image team maintains) and the images that only CI or a test uses (the linters, Hugo’s cimg/go, lychee, Trivy, Docker-in-Docker, busybox, binfmt). Their HIGH and CRITICAL findings are listed and never fail the run. skip: listed, not scanned (the Windows images). The images themselves still come from the files that pin them. To add an image, choose its list: add a line to ci/security-scan-images.txt. An image on no list fails the scan, and lint-circleci runs ci/security-scan.sh lists and fails the pull request that adds it, so the choice is made when the image is added.
What fails. A CRITICAL finding that has a fixed version fails an infra image, and so does an infra image that Trivy cannot scan (the totals name how many are unscannable). The report-only images never fail, because most of them carry some HIGH or CRITICAL finding in any given week, from upstream packages and bundled Go binaries that this repository cannot patch. For every image the log has one line, the end of the log has the totals (infra: 3 images, 0 failing (0 unscannable, … HIGH with a fix reported); report-only: 18 images, 107 CRITICAL and 2097 HIGH with a fix listed), and the artifact findings-.txt lists every HIGH and CRITICAL finding, CRITICAL first, with the installed and the fixed version (- when there is none yet). A finding with no fix yet is counted and never fails. govulncheck is stricter, because the proxy is code that we own: any vulnerability that the proxy calls fails security-scan-go, with a fix or not. The script also stops when its Go is not the Go that builds the proxy (ci/build-proxy.sh and ci/release.sh must name the same version as the job image), so the scan reads what is released.
What to do about a failure. The log ends with the answer: bump the digest (a Renovate pull request does it, Pinned versions), or add a justified .trivyignore entry (the CVE, the reason, an owner and an expiry date: the policy is in that file). An ignore entry also applies to the trivy command of linux-image-example, which reads the same file. Read the tables of the report-only images at your own pace: they are the list of what the next Renovate pull requests, and the next cimg tag, should clear.
Windows images. mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore is listed and skipped. Trivy finds no operating system in a Windows image when it runs on Linux (it returns an empty, clean report), so the scan would claim a result that it does not have. Follow the Microsoft container release notes for Server Core.
Reports. The job stores trivy-.json and findings-.txt for every image, govulncheck-proxy.json, and the summary of each command as artifacts (reports/).
The existing trivy command of linux-image-example is a different check: it gates the image that this repository builds, against its base.
data.stray-claims-timeouts-and-cleanup#Stray: Dedicated resource classes. Nothing else targets the two e2e classes. Serial groups. Host and probes form one job group with a serial-group per project, so two pipelines never run e2e runners at the same time. Both Windows groups share one key, because they share a resource class and token. A group that the filter removes takes its lock jobs with it, and its host and probes are skipped too: they depend only on the lock, and CircleCI does not run a job whose requirements are all filtered out. Evidence and identity. A probe that was not claimed by this workflow’s host fails at its first step. A host whose container exits without the expected probe’s evidence fails at once (the runner idled out, or ran a job that is not ours). Timeouts. Each runner has idle_timeout 5m (every claim happens within seconds, so waiting longer only delays a failure) and max_run_time 10m on Linux and 15m on Windows. The host fails after 40 minutes. Steps have no_output_timeout. A 401 from the runner API fails the host within seconds; the fix is to rotate the token. Cleanup always runs: the stack and secrets are removed and the VM leaves the swarm. A cancel removes the stack. Cancelling an e2e workflow releases the serial-group lock at once, and the idle Swarm service of the cancelled host would claim the B1 of the next pipeline, which fails by design. So the host removes its stack when it is terminated: ci/e2e-host.sh run traps SIGTERM and SIGINT and runs docker stack rm (ci/tests/e2e-sim.sh has a scenario, terminated). ci/E2E-Host.ps1 -Mode Run does the same when PowerShell exits without having ended the run itself (an engine event on PowerShell.Exiting, with a file run-ended that every exit the script chooses writes first, so that a failed run keeps its stack for the logs that Cleanup reads). Windows has no SIGTERM, and a kill that PowerShell cannot see leaves nothing to run, so there the rule is a rerun. Turn “Auto-cancel redundant workflows” off (below), because on a branch that is not the default one every new push cancels the running workflow, and the idle service of the cancelled host is what makes rapid pushes red. Sweep after a failure. If the host fails while a probe may still be queued, it runs a throwaway runner (the pinned official circleci/runner-agent image on Linux; the SHA-256-verified circleci-runner.exe on Windows) for up to 2 minutes so that the probe is claimed and fails fast instead of holding the serial-group lock. If that cannot help (the token was rejected), cancel the workflow in the UI; no API token is kept in the context, so CI cannot cancel workflows itself.

data.the-docker-hub-context#The Docker Hub co:
The context scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub holds two variables for the publication of the token proxy image (The token proxy image):
Variable Value DOCKERHUB_USERNAME The Docker Hub user (or organization service account) that may push to ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy DOCKERHUB_TOKEN An access token of that user with the permission to read and write that repository. Never the password Restrict the context to this project and to main, like the other contexts, so that no other branch, no rerun with SSH and no pipeline started through the API can read the token. Anyone who can push a branch could otherwise add the context to a job of that branch, print the token, and push a malicious image under the tag that the stack files name. Two restrictions, where is the organization slug and is 7bbdbb66-6ba8-4f6c-982e-d4fb401ec257:
circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub --org --type project --value circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub --org --type expression \ --value 'pipeline.git.branch == "main" and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")' The flag is --value (not --restriction-value), and the first command is needed: an expression alone does not tie the context to this project. The live context of this repository has both restrictions already (the maintainers created them with these commands). The CLI cannot list restrictions. Check them in the web app (Organization Settings, then Contexts, then the context), or with the API: curl --header "circle-token: ${CIRCLECI_TOKEN}" https://circleci.com/api/v2/context//restrictions (the id is in the output of circleci context list --org ). It must show one project and one expression restriction.
Only jobs that run on main carry the context (the publish variants of the image jobs, proxy-image-publish, proxy-image-edge and release), and the setup phase never attaches it. Until both values exist, a pipeline that is not the production main pushes nothing and stays green: the image jobs build and test, then print NOT PUSHED with the reason, and the release builds its bundle but does not create the release. On the production main (both e2e tokens present) the missing values fail those jobs (Publishing fails closed on main).
data.the-e2e-context-and-smr-swarm#The e2e co:
The context scalable-machine-runner-e2e holds the runner tokens, and its restriction names main and every branch that starts with smr-swarm/ (Secrets and public logs). The configuration of a job comes from its own branch, so anyone who can push a branch named smr-swarm/anything can change .circleci/ in it, print the tokens in a public log, and read them. That is a deliberate trade for the time that the e2e work lives on a branch of its own. The maintainers have set the second ruleset (step 3 below) before the first release, and the end of the trade is this list:
After the merge, rotate both runner tokens (circleci runner token create --nickname ci-YYYYMM, replace the secret in the context, delete the old token: Troubleshooting). Any token that a branch could read before is untrusted. Limit the context to main, or to exact branch names: change the when of setup-e2e in .circleci/config.yml, the expression restriction of the context, eligible in ci/setup-gate.sh and the rows of ci/tests/setup-gate.sh and ci/tests/setup-config.sh. Restrict who can create the branches with a second ruleset: target smr-swarm/**, Restrict creations and Restrict updates, and a bypass list of the maintainers only. A stranger’s push then cannot create a branch that the context accepts. Until the context is limited to main, the ruleset is what keeps the tokens in the hands of the maintainers.
data.the-e2e-simulation#The e2e simulation: ci/tests/e2e-sim.sh runs ci/e2e-host.sh and ci/e2e-probe.sh in a privileged docker:dind container with a fake runner that runs the next queued probe as an unprivileged user and exits 0, as a single-task runner does. Swarm, the stack deploy, the restart policy, docker events, the secrets and the evidence handling are real. Three scenarios: pass, no job queued (the host must fail with “exited without evidence”), and a probe failure (the host must fail). It also checks that the token never reaches the output. The e2e-simulation job runs it in about 2 minutes; run it before changing the e2e scripts, so that a real e2e run is not spent on a typo.
data.the-heavy-suites#The heavy suites:
Three suites cost most of a pipeline, and a change to the shell scripts of Linux or to a README does not need them. The setup gate switches them on from the files that the push changes (ci/changed-files.sh):
Parameter Jobs Runs on main and with full: true, and on any other branch when a changed path is windows windows-swarm-ltsc2022 windows/, ci/, .circleci/ or PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 proxy-image proxy-image-linux, proxy-image-windows-ltsc2022 proxy/, ci/, .circleci/ or windows/tests/ microvm linux-microvm linux/stack/, linux/tests/, docs/microvm.md, ci/ or .circleci/ ci/ and .circleci/ are in every row: they hold the scripts and the jobs of all the suites. When the changed files are not known (the first build of a branch, a pipeline started through the API), every suite runs, as for documentation-only changes. full-suite is for main and full: true only: the Windows Server 2025 jobs (windows-swarm-ltsc2025, proxy-image-windows-ltsc2025) and linux-mixed-arch. A branch such as smr-swarm/* gets neither. ci/tests/setup-gate.sh has the table of paths and the answers that the gate must print.
To get everything on a branch, for example before a risky merge, start a pipeline for it with the parameter full: true. A schedule that sets full: true on main or on a branch gives a nightly full run. Neither runs the e2e or the release job: only main does.
data.troubleshooting#Troubleshooting: Symptom Cause and fix e2e-*-b1 stays queued and the host job failed The sweep could not claim it (the token was rejected, or Docker Hub was unreachable). Cancel the workflow in the UI; the serial-group lock is then released Host fails with “token was rejected (401)” Rotate the token: circleci runner token create --nickname ci-YYYYMM, update the context secret, delete the old token Host fails with “container for probe bN exited without evidence” The runner idled out without claiming the probe, or claimed someone else’s job on the e2e class. Check the probe job’s status and e2e/logs/service.log (the runner output) in the artifacts Probe fails “not claimed by the e2e host of workflow …” A runner outside this workflow holds the e2e token, or the host’s sweeper claimed the probe on purpose after a failure. A third cause: cancelling an e2e workflow releases the serial-group lock at once, but the cancelled host VM’s idle Swarm service can live on for a few minutes and claim the next pipeline’s B1, which fails here by design. The Linux host removes its stack when it is terminated, and a Windows host when PowerShell sees the end, so this should be rare. Check that Auto-cancel redundant workflows is off (Secrets and public logs), and rerun the workflow The job fails and the runner log says failed to remove working directory or could not clean up task, with permission denied Only if CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR is true on a Linux service; the entrypoint and the stack files default it to false. See Error: failed to remove working directory Test-StopHandling.ps1 or the e2e fails with a container exit code of 3221225786 A container that ran a job was ended about 5 seconds after a stop from outside. The e2e never stops a busy container, so look for something else that stopped the stack (a second pipeline, a cleanup that ran too early). Check reports/stop-*.txt Test-Injection.ps1 fails tar-agent-style GNU tar from the mounted Git failed on the operands the task agent passes (forward slashes, --force-local, MSYS=winsymlinks:nativestrict). Read the check’s detail in reports/injection-*.txt; the e2e’s workspace round trip is the end-to-end proof setup says an e2e group is skipped The context is missing, or lacks the secret. The log says which token is absent. Only the setup-e2e workflow (main and smr-swarm/*) has the context at all setup of main or smr-swarm/* fails with an authorization error The context’s expression restriction refused the pipeline: it was started through the API, or it is an SSH rerun. Push a commit, or rerun without SSH A Windows step fails right after docker swarm init with Unable to connect to the remote server or no such host The network drops for a few seconds after the swarm is created. Download and pull first A Windows host step hangs instead of failing A child process started with -NoNewWindow (docker events, docker service logs) keeps the step’s console open. E2E-Host.ps1 kills the child process trees on every failure path; keep that if it changes A Windows step dies with NativeCommandError on a harmless warning In Windows PowerShell 5.1 a native command’s stderr redirected with 2>&1 under $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' is a terminating error. Run docker through Invoke-Docker in E2E-Host.ps1 Trivy fails with “no space left on device” /tmp on the machine image is too small for a large image tarball plus Trivy’s Java DB. The trivy command keeps both under $HOME/trivy lint-stack, linux-swarm or the release job fails with config machine-runner-swarm-... is stale A file that a Swarm config carries (the entrypoint or a distributor script) changed, and the name in the stack files did not. Run ci/config-names.sh --write and commit the new names. Refer to Swarm config names lint-shell fails with SC2154 on an uppercase variable .shellcheckrc enables check-unassigned-uppercase. Assign the variable (${NAME:-}) or add a # shellcheck disable=SC2154 with the reason

data.what-a-windows-pass-looks-like#What a Wi:
Every Windows test prints CHECK PASS|FAIL lines and one RESULT ... line, and exits 0 only on a pass. A CircleCI PowerShell step does not stop on a failed native command by itself, so ci\Invoke-Test.ps1 checks the exit code of each test. The CHECK details in the reports are the evidence.
Test Final line (shape) What it proves Test-Injection.ps1 RESULT injection mode=injected ... verdict=PASS OS build, the runner and Git mounts (read-only), toolchain (bash, GNU tar, administrator, symlink privilege), tar-agent-style (the flags and forward-slash operands of the task agent), long paths, the default PATH, exit 80, the config file, and with -Online a real start of the runner with a bogus token. NOTE lines record the exit code of a missing config file (1) Test-Ephemerality.ps1 RESULT mode=restart-policy jobs=3 distinct_containers=1 jobs_with_residue=2, then RESULT mode=swarm jobs=3 distinct_containers=3 jobs_with_residue=0 The negative control (a plain docker --restart reuses the container and sees residue) and a stack with restart_policy: any (a new container each time) Test-Exit80.ps1 RESULT exit80 ... swarm_exits=<2..8> window=60s delay=10s verdict=PASS Exit 80 for a missing name, token or an invalid name, and no hot loop under Swarm (about 70 s) Test-Placement.ps1 RESULT placement ... host_tag=ltsc2022 verdict=PASS Constrained services stay pending until the node has the label (about 2 to 4 min) Test-StopHandling.ps1 -Online RESULT stop ... job_seconds=40 verdict=PASS The real runner drains on docker stop and exits 0, and a Swarm secret is read as the runner config. A NOTE control line shows that a busy stock container is KILLED by a stop (job_finished=False, exit 3221225786, about 6 s) Test-Install.ps1 RESULT install checks=7 failed=0 stack=runners verdict=PASS The distributor of the shipped stack installs the release that the stack pins, which the real manifest lists, with the SHA-256 record, the two relative links, and Git, and the stock mounts run circleci-runner.exe, git, bash and GNU tar and are read-only (the first download takes minutes) Test-Distributor.ps1 RESULT distributor checks= failed=0 verdict=PASS The script in a Server Core container against a mirror read through file:// URLs: a pin, the record, 3.1 and 3 as the newest of their line, the arm64 file names, current resolved by SHA-256, the major-version guard, a rollback with the mirror gone, a wrong SHA-256 and a list that holds the right one, pruning to 3, a changed binary replaced, and a container that keeps its version while current moves and keeps its version directory from removal Test-Persistent.ps1 RESULT persistent ... verdict=PASS Continuous mode: one long-lived container, and a named volume that survives its replacement (about 2 min)
data.what-each-job-can-see#What each job can:
The project is public and a branch pusher chooses the configuration that a job of that branch runs, so what matters is which job holds which secret. A context attaches to a job by name, and a job without a context sees none of these values. This is the complete list:
Job Context Secrets in its environment Runs on setup, in the workflow setup-e2e scalable-machine-runner-e2e E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_LINUX, E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_WINDOWS. The job only checks that they are not empty main and smr-swarm/* setup, in setup-plain and setup-scan None None Every other branch, and the weekly scan The e2e host jobs: e2e-linux-host, e2e-linux-arm64-host, and the Windows hosts scalable-machine-runner-e2e Both e2e tokens (a host uses the one of its operating system) main and smr-swarm/*, when the token is present The e2e probe jobs e2e-*-b1, -b2, -b3 None None. They are ordinary jobs that the runner of the host claims, and they run the code of the branch The same proxy-image-linux-publish, proxy-image-windows-*-publish, proxy-image-publish, proxy-image-edge scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub DOCKERHUB_USERNAME, DOCKERHUB_TOKEN main release scalable-machine-runner-release and scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub GITHUB_TOKEN of the release (Contents: Read and write), DOCKERHUB_USERNAME, DOCKERHUB_TOKEN main, with both e2e tokens present docs-site-publish scalable-machine-runner-docs GITHUB_TOKEN of the docs (Contents: Read and write) main docs-site-comment scalable-machine-runner-pr-comments GITHUB_PR_COMMENT_TOKEN A push that has a pull request, on any branch Every other job None None Three things the table does not show:
Every job can get an OIDC token, with no context (circleci run oidc get: signing-rehearsal does). The token proves the project and the branch, which is why the signature check reads the ref (How the signature works). The setup jobs also hold the continuation key of their pipeline, which can only continue that pipeline. A job on main runs the code of main. Whoever can change .circleci/ or ci/ on main controls what runs with each of these secrets. That is why main needs the ruleset below. The docs token reaches as far as the release token. Both are Contents: Read and write on the whole repository. The separate context decides which job can use the docs token, and not what it can do. docs-site-publish also downloads and runs third-party code at build time (Hugo, the Hextra module, a Mermaid script), which the project pins by version and checksum, while it holds that token. The ruleset on main (no bypass, a pull request required) is what stops that token from changing main.

data.when-things-run-and-the-setup-gate#When:
Branch or trigger Setup workflow Parameters set by setup Jobs any branch other than the two below setup-plain, no context windows, proxy-image and microvm for the changed files that each suite reads (below) the every pipeline and not docs-only rows, and those suites the same, with the pipeline parameter full: true (API call or a schedule) setup-plain, no context full-suite, and the three heavy suites adds the Server 2025 jobs, linux-mixed-arch and every heavy suite. Never e2e, never release smr-swarm/* setup-e2e, with the e2e context the heavy suites for the changed files, as on any branch; e2e-linux and e2e-windows for the tokens that are present the e2e groups. The Server 2025 jobs and linux-mixed-arch do not run here main setup-e2e, with the e2e context full-suite, windows, proxy-image, microvm adds the Server 2025 jobs, linux-mixed-arch and every heavy suite main with E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_LINUX present setup-e2e adds e2e-linux adds the Linux e2e group main with E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_WINDOWS present setup-e2e adds e2e-windows adds the Windows e2e groups main with both tokens setup-e2e adds release and strict adds the release job and proxy-image-edge, and a missing publishing credential fails (below) main (with or without the tokens) setup-e2e adds publish swaps the token proxy image jobs for their publish variants, with the Docker Hub context, and adds proxy-image-publish any of the above, when the push changes documentation only (below) the same workflow docs-only, and full-suite, the heavy suites, e2e-*, publish and release off (strict stays) the lint jobs and docs-site-build only the schedule of the security scan setup-scan, no context security-scan the workflow security-scan only a tag none runs a job nothing nothing: the setup job has no tag filter, so CircleCI runs no job for the tag The two setup workflows for pushes are exclusive: setup-e2e has when the branch is main or starts with smr-swarm/, and setup-plain has when it is not. The setup job of setup-e2e has the scalable-machine-runner-e2e context attached, which holds the runner tokens, and the job of setup-plain has no context at all, so the tokens exist in no job of any other branch. A job of another branch could otherwise name the e2e runner class and read the token of the runner that claims it. The e2e jobs are added to the pipeline only when the context’s job sees a non-empty E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_LINUX or E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_WINDOWS. Without the context or its secrets the pipeline still runs lint, builds and the local tests, and stays green. The third workflow, setup-scan, runs only when the pipeline parameter security-scan is true, on whatever branch the schedule names, and the other two do not run then: the scan never has the e2e context, not even on main.
The decision lives in ci/setup-gate.sh, which the setup job calls with --e2e true (the job with the context) or --e2e false (the plain job, which never enables e2e, whatever its environment holds) and the full parameter. Two tests keep it honest, both in lint-circleci:
ci/tests/setup-gate.sh is a table of branches, contexts, parameters and tokens, and the parameters the gate must print. It needs only bash and jq. ci/tests/setup-config.sh compiles .circleci/config.yml with circleci config process for a table of branch names and checks that exactly one setup workflow is left, that the e2e context appears only for main and smr-swarm/*, and that every other branch gets a job without a context and with --e2e false.
data.windows#Windows:
e2e-windows-2022 (job group, serial-group /e2e-windows) e2e-windows-2022-host (A), -b1, -b2, -b3 e2e-windows-2025 (the same group on Server 2025, requires e2e-windows-2022) The host (ci/E2E-Host.ps1) follows the same shape, with one service and three probes:
Prepare pulls the stock image, runs windows\Setup.ps1 -InitSwarm -AdvertiseAddr (docker swarm init and the node label), and then deploys the shipped stack with no runner replicas until its distributor has installed the runner and Git from the real manifest. It removes the stack again; the volume stays. See the facts above for the order. Run takes the shipped windows/stack/runners.yaml as text, replaces ltsc2022 with the host’s tag (ltsc2025 on Server 2025), layers an override on it (one replica of windows-default on the stock image, an idle timeout, the evidence mount). runners.yaml holds only windows-default: the optional classes are the add-on stack files persistent.yaml, custom-image.yaml and docker-build.yaml, and the e2e deploys none of them, and deploys it with --resolve-image never (the image is local). The Swarm secret windows-default-token is the runner config file (api: with auth_token: under it), built from E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_WINDOWS, and only the token proxy mounts it; the runner reads runner-placeholder-token. The windows/amd64 proxy of proxy-test is installed by the distributor from a local mirror (C:\e2e-proxy, a bind mount). Each probe’s MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_INSTANCE_ID must equal the Swarm task ID of the container that Swarm started for it (the stack sets the variable to {{.Task.ID}}), and the computer name must be that container’s ID. The host stops its docker events and docker service logs followers before it exits: a child started with -NoNewWindow keeps the step’s console open, and the step would hang until its no_output_timeout. The probes plant residue in the user profile, %TEMP%, C:\ProgramData, C:\Users\Public, the registry (HKLM:\SOFTWARE\SwarmE2E) and the machine environment (SWARM_TEST_E2E). Windows has no step-down: the runner and the jobs are the same account, so the probe records, and does not assert, whether the job can read the token. Normal flow only. Every probe’s job finishes by itself, and every container exits 0 after its job. The e2e does not stop a busy container: on stock Server Core that kills the job after about 5 seconds, which Test-StopHandling.ps1 measures and Stop a busy Windows container explains. Workspace and cache, with real jobs (ci/E2E-Storage.ps1). B1 creates a file tree (a text file, directories tmp and test-results, t.txt, a symbolic link) and a cache file, records their SHA-256 sums outside the workspace, and runs persist_to_workspace and save_cache. B2 runs attach_workspace and restore_cache and compares every sum; the link must arrive as a link or a copy with the same content. The host prints workspace=ok cache=ok symlink=... and which tar the agent used (use_go_tar: when false, the workspace goes through Git’s tar.exe and gzip in the container, the path that the stack’s Git mount exists for). Not covered by the e2e. The persistent (continuous) class runs only in Test-Persistent.ps1 and linux/tests, without real jobs. The e2e stack leaves hostname: unset on Windows: a fixed hostname would make COMPUTERNAME identical across the containers of a slot and defeat the probes (and a Windows computer name is limited to 15 characters).
data.windows-jobs#Windows jobs:
windows-swarm runs on the stock Server Core image. There is no entrypoint script: the runner (circleci-runner.exe machine --config C:\ProgramData\Docker\secrets\circleci_runner_config.yaml) is the container’s main process, and the runner and portable Git come from the read-only mounts C:\machine-runner-swarm and C:\Program Files\Git of the volume runner-bin, which the distributor of the stack fills. The steps are:
Engine check: docker info must report OSType windows. Windows PowerShell 5.1 unit tests (Invoke-UnitTests.ps1, Pester 5.7.1; the image registers both a Nuget and a PSGallery repository, so modules are installed with -Repository PSGallery). docker pull of the stock image, then windows\Setup.ps1 -InitSwarm -AdvertiseAddr (docker swarm init and the machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc* node labels). Pulling comes first because the network is down for a few seconds after the swarm is created. Then Test-Install.ps1 deploys the shipped stack with no runner replicas, so that the distributor installs the runner and Git from the real manifest, and checks what it installed. The volume stays for the tests that follow.
